match.reason: The closest bank point, Language features suit audience and purpose, is broader because it centres on audience as well as purpose and does not teach the report, persuasive and story contrast (technical words and facts, emotive words and opinions, description and dialogue) that this point needs, so a new point is the safer match.

draft.title: Language features change with purpose
card: A report informs. It uses technical words, such as habitat or predator, and facts that can be checked.
A persuasive text tries to change what a reader thinks. It uses emotive words, which stir feelings, and opinions.
A story entertains. It uses description to build a picture and dialogue, which is the words characters speak.
Writers choose words to suit the job the text must do.
draft.remember: The words a writer picks match what the text is trying to do.

a.q: Which sentence would most likely come from a persuasive text?
opts: Our heartless council must stop this cruel waste now
The council collects bins on Tuesday each week
The bin truck rumbled slowly down the quiet street
First, place the bin on the kerb before sunrise
a.why: Heartless and cruel are emotive words, and the sentence gives an opinion about what should happen. The bin collection sentence states a fact, which suits a report.
a.clue: Look for words meant to stir feelings.

b.q: Omar writes two sentences about penguins. The first says they are flightless birds of the Southern Hemisphere. The second says their flippers help them swim. What is the main purpose shown by this language?
b.why: The sentences state facts that can be checked and use no feelings or opinions. That suits a report that informs. Persuasive writing would add emotive words or opinions.

a.best: Our heartless council must stop this cruel waste now
